searchText: Hi everyone! I'm trying to run the web3 tests on the deposit contract in the eth2.0specs repository (https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/tree/dev/solidity_deposit_contract), and I'm running in to a python import error with `py_ecc`: py_ecc import error Anyone know how to get past this one? Can't find anything with google. I'm running this on an intel macbook pro with big sur Sorry if this is the wrong place for the question! There is a make build command for the deposit contract tests, I believe On mobile. Let me see Yup, I ran the make command for the contract itself, I think I have that working already, just trying to get the tests to run Currently stuck on the command `make test_deposit_contract_web3_tests` Did you run make install_deposit_contract_tester? Ah Yup, got that working too Run make install_test And make build You need to build the executable pyspec Which looks like that import is failing Ok, I'll give that a try 😄 If you have any recommendations for the readme, please feel free to open a pr. There are a few people that run this stuff all the time and dont ever look at the instructions. Fresh eyes can make it better! Well I've run into a couple of issues with building the tester tools itself, I was thinking about opening an issue for that but I wasn't sure if its just a problem with my environment had to make two changes to get the tester target to build Here's my diff so far: tester diff fixes this issue: tried `make build`, but I don't think there's a target for `build` in the `Makefile` Ah but I do see a `test` target in the Makefile, `make test` seems to be compiling something, I think I'll be able to run the pytest after that Ah make pyspec Sorry Gotcha. Well, I'm still stuck on the py_ecc import error after pyspec. Not sure what's goin on, but I appreciate the help
